title: Pulled Pork Sandwiches
subtitle: Slow-smoked pull, soft buns, fast line
description: Sandwich line for the whole hall

steps.title: Rub & slow-cook pork (low, 4 hr)
steps.instruction: Season shoulder, slow cook until pull-apart tender. Rest 20 min, then shred.

steps.title: Toss pork with sauce (low, 15 min)
steps.instruction: Mix shredded pork with BBQ sauce; hold warm. Watch color and texture — if it smells sharp or looks pale, give it another minute before moving on.

steps.title: Warm beans & toast buns (medium, 12 min)
steps.instruction: Heat beans with extra sauce; warm split buns on sheet pan. Watch color and texture — if it smells sharp or looks pale, give it another minute before moving on.

steps.title: Toss coleslaw (no heat, 8 min)
steps.instruction: Dress slaw just before line opens so it stays crisp. Watch color and texture — if it smells sharp or looks pale, give it another minute before moving on.

steps.title: Run the sandwich line (serve)
steps.instruction: Bun, pork, slaw, pickles — crew adds extra sauce if they want.

proTips: Start pork early — shoulder needs time more than attention.
Keep slaw cold until the last minute.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Pulled Pork Sandwiches with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Pulled Pork Sandwiches on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Store components separate — assemble fresh; buns go soggy overnight.
